title: The Object QML Collected: Who Owns What a C++ Function Hands to JavaScript

questions.question: An invokable returns a new QObject with no parent. Who owns it?
questions.explanation: The garbage collector deletes it when the JavaScript value is unreachable. Alive went from 3 to 2 after a collection.

questions.question: C++ keeps a raw pointer to that object in a member. What is it after a collection?
questions.explanation: The pointer C++ kept was gone.

questions.question: What does CppOwnership with no parent mean?
options: Nobody deletes it unless C++ does
questions.explanation: It leaks. The test had to delete it by hand.

questions.question: What does reading an object from a Q_PROPERTY give?
options: An object QML does not own
questions.explanation: It is not collected. The held object was alive after the collection.

questions.question: What does keep_alive set?
questions.explanation: There is one owner in C++. The pooled objects had the pool as parent and CppOwnership.

questions.question: Why is a pool not enough by itself?
options: It never decides an object is finished
questions.explanation: Something must clear it. The lesson says so under what it does not do.
